newsitem.title: UK: Brazil to keep sugar exports at 5.0 mln tonnes.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to keep sugar exports at 5.0 mln tonnes.

text.p: Brazil, the world's top sugar grower, will maintain its sugar exports at 5.0 million tonnes a year despite growing local supplies, a senior government official said on Friday.

Mauricio Assis, the head of the Industry and Commerce Ministry's primary commodities department, told reporters in London that any excess sugar cane supplies would be used in alcohol production to substitute imports.
Brazil produces about 14 million tonnes of cane sugar a year.
"We will maintain our sugar exports and decrease alcohol imports," said Assis, who is in London for a visit.
"We will not contemplate to increase sugar exports," he said.
Brazil now imports about half a billion litres of sugar alcohols, used as auto fuel, a year mainly from Europe.
Annual alcohol production is pegged at 12.5 billion litres against demand of 13 billion.
Assis also said Brazil planned to replace some low-yielding sugar cane crop with other profitable crops. He did not elaborate. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
